title: L-Type Ca2+ Current Protocol
author: Robert Harvey
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ba8mihu6

steps.title: Prepare Cell and Perfusion Chamber
steps.instruction: Place isolated rat ventricular myocytes in a perfusion chamber (Warner Instruments) on the stage of an inverted microscope (Olympus IX71).

substeps.instruction: Bathe cells in a K+-free extracellular solution containing (in mM): NaCl 137, CsCl 5.4, MgCl2 0.5, CaCl2 1.0, NaH2PO4 0.33, glucose 5.5, and HEPES 5 (pH 7.4).
Maintain the solution at room temperature.

steps.title: Establish Whole-Cell Configuration
steps.instruction: Patch cells using the whole-cell configuration of the patch clamp technique.

substeps.instruction: Use microelectrodes with resistances between 1 and 2 MΩ.
Dialyze cells with a K+-free microelectrode solution containing (in mM): CsCl 130, TEA-Cl 20, EGTA 5, MgATP 5, TrisGTP 0.06, and HEPES 5 (pH 7.2).
Compensate access resistance to ensure series resistance errors are less than 5 mV.

steps.title: Configure Data Acquisition System
steps.instruction: Set up voltage-clamp recording using a Multiclamp 700B amplifier, Digidata 1440A interface, and pClamp 11 software.

substeps.instruction: Apply a low-pass filter at 4 kHz.

steps.title: Establish Baseline and Voltage Protocol
steps.instruction: Obtain a stable baseline for approximately 5 minutes before applying test drugs using the following voltage-clamp protocol:

substeps.instruction: Apply a 50 ms pre-pulse to -40 mV to inactivate Na+ channels.
Apply a 100 ms test pulse to 0 mV to elicit the L-type Ca2+ current.

steps.title: Monitor Ca2+ Current Amplitude
steps.instruction: Monitor the time course of changes in the Ca2+ current amplitude.

substeps.instruction: Record the amplitude of the peak inward current elicited during the test pulse to 0 mV.
Apply the test pulse once every 5 s.
